questions.q:
Which of the following statement(s) is (are) correct?
(i) $\mathrm{LiF}$ is less soluble in water
(ii) $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is less ionic than $\mathrm{CsCl}$
(iii) Formation of alkali metal halide is an endothermic reaction
questions.solution:
LiF being predominantly covalent, has a high lattice enthalpy due to which it is less soluble in water. Thus, (i) is correct.
$\mathrm{Na}^{+} \lt  \mathrm{Cs}^{+}$so the polarizing power of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$is higher than that of $\mathrm{Cs}^{+}$which results in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ being more covalent or less ionic than $\mathrm{CsCl}$.
Thus, (ii) is also correct.
Formation of alkali metal halides like $\mathrm{NaCl}, \mathrm{CsCl}, \mathrm{KF}$, etc. is an exothermic reaction which gives rise to a stable crystal lattice.
Thus, (iii) is incorrect.

(ii) $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ is less soluble in water than $\mathrm{CaSO}_4$
(iii) Alkaline earth metals do not dissolve in liquid ammonia

$4 \mathrm{Li} \mathrm{NO}_3 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{Li}_2 \mathrm{O}+4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2$ (anomalous behaviour)
$2 \mathrm{Ba}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_2 \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{BaO}+4 \mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{O}_2$
Thus, (i) is correct.
The solubility of alkaline earth metals decreases down the group due to a decrease in hydration enthalpy compared to the lattice enthalpy.
Thus, $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ will be less soluble in water than $\mathrm{CaSO}_4$. Thus, (ii) is also correct.
Alkaline earth metals dissolve in liquid ammonia to form a coloured solution.
$\mathrm{M}+(\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}) \mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow\left[\mathrm{M}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_{\mathrm{x}}\right]^{2+}+2\left[\mathrm{e}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_{\mathrm{y}}\right]^{-}$
Thus, (iii) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lithium shows diagonal relationship with element '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>' and aluminum with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mo>.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi></math> respectively are
questions.solution:
A diagonal relationship is said to exist between certain pairs of diagonally adjacent elements in the second and third periods (first 20 elements) of the periodic table.These pairs lithium and magnesium, beryllium and aluminum, boron and silicon, etc.). These similarities in the properties of diagonally adjacent elements are due to the similar polarizing power, similar ionic charge to size ratio of diagonally adjacent elements.
Hence, lithium shows diagonal relationship with magnesium and aluminium shows diagonal relationship with beryllium.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of the metallic character of the elements <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Be</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Al</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Na</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> is
questions.solution:
Metallic character decreases as we move across a period in the periodic table from left to right. This occurs as atoms more readily accept electrons to fill a valence shell than lose them to remove the unfilled shell. Metallic character increases as we move down an element group in the periodic table.

Potassium belongs to 4th period, sodium and aluminium belong to 3rd period, beryllium belongs to 2nd period in the periodic table. Hence, their correct metallic character is K>Na>Al>Be.

options: A and R both are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R both are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is incorrect but R is correct
questions.solution: For a compound to be soluble in water, hydration enthapy must dominate over the lattice enthalpy. In MgSO4, Mg2+ being smaller in size, hydration enthalpy dominates over the lattice enthalpy of MgSO4. Hence, MgSO4 is readily soluble in water.

The reaction of potassium cyanide with sodium hydroxide gives the cyanide ion. After that cyanide ion reacts with the thiosulphate ions and cool and acidify in presence of the hydrochloric acid. It gives the thiocyanide ion.

KCN + NaOH→NaCN + KOH

 S2O32- +CN- →HClSCN- + SO3-

The thiocyanate ion reacts with the iron (III) chloride and formed the Fe(SCN)2+ and the complex has the blood-red colour.

FeCl3  +SCN-→ Fe(SCN)2+(blood red colour)

Hence, the solution is cooled and acidified with HCl and this solution with iron (III) chloride produces blood-red colour solution.

ii. Group II elements dissolve in liquid ammonia to form deep blue-black solutions.
iii. The hydration enthalpy of group II ions decreases from \(\mathrm{Be}^{2+}\) to \(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}\).
questions.solution:
All the given statements are correct and their explanations are as follows:
(i) Berylium oxide is an amphoteric oxide, i.e. it can react with both acids and bases.
(ii) Group II elements dissolve in liquid ammonia to form deep blue solutions. This blue colour of the solution is due to the ammoniated electron which absorbs energy in the visible region of light and thus impart blue colour to solution.
\(M+(x+y) \mathrm{NH}_3 \longrightarrow\left[M\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_x\right]^{2+}+2\left[e\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_y\right]\)
(iii) The hydration enthalpy of group II ions decreases from \(\mathrm{Be}^{2+}\) to \(\mathrm{Ba}^{2+}\), as the size of cation increases down the group.

Given,
A compound \(\left(\mathrm{MO}_2\right)\) of group 1 element \((M)\) hydrolysed to give \(\mathrm{M}^{+}, \mathrm{OH}^{-}, X\) and \(Y\) when \((X)\) reacts with \(\mathrm{I}_2\) in basic medium, it gives \(\mathrm{I}^{-}\), water and \((Y)\). The reaction involved are as follows :
\(\begin{aligned}
& 2 \mathrm{MO}_2+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{M}^{+}+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \\
& (X) \\
& \mathrm{I}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}^{-}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}_2
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following reactions are correct with respect to the formation of products?
I. $2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{SO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+\mathrm{H}_2$
II. $2 \mathrm{XeF}_4+3 \mathrm{O}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2 \stackrel{143 \mathrm{~K}}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{XeO}_3+7 \mathrm{~F}_2$
III. $\mathrm{PCl}_5+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4+5 \mathrm{HCl}$
IV. $2 \mathrm{NaNO}_2+2 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
questions.solution:
For the given reactions :
(I) $2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{SO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4+\mathrm{H}_2$ is not correct. The correct reaction is

2 \mathrm{NaOH}+\mathrm{SO}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}

(II) $2 \mathrm{XeF}_4+3 \mathrm{O}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2 \stackrel{143 \mathrm{~K}}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{XeO}_3+7 \mathrm{~F}_2$ is also not the correct reaction, the correct reaction is

\mathrm{XeF}_4+\mathrm{O}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2 \stackrel{143 \mathrm{~K}}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{XeF}_6+\mathrm{O}_2

(III) $\mathrm{PCl}_5+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4+5 \mathrm{HCl}$ is the correct reaction, if occurs in two steps, as follows:
(i) $\mathrm{PCl}_5+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{POCl}_3+2 \mathrm{HCl}$
(ii) $\mathrm{POCl}_3+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4+3 \mathrm{HCl}$
Overall reaction,

\mathrm{PCl}_5+4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{PO}_4+5 \mathrm{HCl}

(IV) $2 \mathrm{NaNO}_2+2 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{NO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is also the correct reaction as $\mathrm{HCl}$ can decomposes salts like $\mathrm{NaNO}_2$ to $\mathrm{NaCl}, \mathrm{NO}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.
Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: Superoxides are the species having an $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}$ bond and $\mathrm{O}$ in an oxidation state of $-\frac{1}{2}$ (superoxide ion is $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$). Usually these are formed by active metals such as $\mathrm{KO}_2, \mathrm{RbO}_2$ and $\mathrm{CsO}_2$. For the salts of larger anions (like $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$), lattice energy increases in a group. Since, lattice energy is the driving force for the formation of an ionic compound and its stability, the stability of the superoxides from ' $\mathrm{K}$ ' to 'Cs' also increases.
